subject: Help for plotting relative rather than count data

messages.author: 2401d0740178cf07
messages.subject: Help for plotting relative rather than count data
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to produce frequency plots of my data. So far I was able
to plot count data, but I couldn't find a way to plot relative
frequency, despite geom_density's documentation richness of details.

Basically, my data is composed by multi-year maps containing rates
of deforestation which range from 0 to 1. My objective is, for each
year, to slice data into deforestation thresholds and count the
frequency of cells within each slice.

Below I am pasting the code I have written (with some help from R-
SIG-GEO discussion list). In order to be able reproduce this code, I
gently invite you to download this sample data file:
https://www.dropbox.com/sh/9hslhmoq2e8zwrs/VR1iB2EsU9/defor-3-years.nc

#Load required packages
library (raster)
library (reshape)
library (ggplot2)

#Load data
deforest <- brick("/home/thiago/Dropbox/defor-3-years.nc")

#Probe layer names and plot raster data (Optional step)
layerNames(deforest)
plot(deforest)

#Convert spatial object to data frame
meltR <- melt(as.array(deforest))

#Define classes used to count grids
meltR$class <- cut(meltR$value, c(0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8,1))

#Define factors to plot individual years
meltR$X3 <- factor(meltR$X3, labels=c("2000","2001","2002"))

#Discard NA values
meltR <- na.omit(meltR)

#Plot data
p <- ggplot(meltR,aes(x=class))
p + geom_histogram(aes(fill=class)) + facet_grid(. ~ X3)

This code produces nice, informative histograms plots. However, I am
trying to display relative counts. Could you give me a little hand?

Thanks in advance for your time and help.

Best wishes,
Thiago Veloso.

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Help for plotting relative rather than count data
parts:
Hi Thiago,

I'm not sure what you mean by "relative counts", but here is my guess
as to what you are looking for:

library(plyr)

meltR.prop <- ddply(meltR, "X3", function(DF) {
as.data.frame(prop.table(table(DF$class)))
}
)

ggplot(meltR.prop, aes(x = Var1, y = Freq*100, fill = Var1)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
facet_grid(. ~ X3)

Best,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: Help for plotting relative rather than count data
parts:
Hi Ista,

Thanks very much for your quick answer and efficient solution.

Your suggestion yielded exactly what I needed. You are right - with
"relative counts" I mean proportion of that amount relative to the
whole. For example, considering a sample of 100 values, if 40 values
are distributed across the first 'class' (from 0 to 0.2), then this
class bar would indicate 40.

Is there any way to achieve the same results using only ggplot2
package?

Best,
Thiago.
